name: The Sundering
summary: The fixed point of Vaelorian history. In a single year, the Song Unbinding completed what nine centuries of divine war had begun: the Veil tore along a north-east to south-west seam, the song shattered, magic turned wild or died, the Quiet opened, and the kingdoms of the Concord fell within months. A third of all Weavers died, a third went mad, and a third walked silent into the Quiet. The gods did not return. Every calendar on Aurelith now counts from this year.

participants.name: the-high-concord
participants.note: spoke the Song Unbinding believing control was possible

participants.name: the-unbinding
participants.note: their texts armed the catastrophe; their members were its first casualties

participants.name: mornath
participants.note: walked out last at winter's end; the Veil-Keepers keep his vigil

participants.name: all peoples of Aurelith
participants.note: every living culture descends from someone who survived this year

course_of_events.what: The Veil tears along a north-east to south-west seam. Where it passes, magic dies and sound follows — villages report the world going mute for days. Karvess vitrifies in a single hour, mid-morning. The Quiet opens as a permanent wound.
Weavers everywhere are struck by visions of the un-sung song. A third die outright. A third go mad. A third go silent and walk into the Quiet — walking, witnesses insist, willingly and in step.
The Concord's great kingdoms collapse within weeks. Glass cities shatter; woven bridges fail; refugees flee toward the world's edges. Solmere does not yet exist; Karvess is already glass.
Survivors of the High Concord gather in Velkash's broken thread-quarter and swear the oath: contain the Glimmer forever. Each carries a censer of ash from the burned Colleges.
Mornath departs last. The Veil reaches its thinnest recorded state. The first Stilleven silence is observed across the world — and has been observed every year since.

key_places.name: The Quiet
key_places.description: The rent itself: a scar of cracked earth and silver mist running from the Stone Crown to the Burning Sands, advancing a hand's width most years. Within it the Glimmer does not answer — and something listens.

key_places.name: Karvess
key_places.description: The glass kingdom, vitrified mid-morning on the Rent's first day. Towers, fountains, ten thousand people preserved translucent. It hums on quiet nights.

key_places.name: Velkash's Broken Thread-Quarter
key_places.description: Where the First Censer swore its oath among still-smoldering silk works. Rebuilt twice since; the oath-stones remain in the Censer Quarter's foundation.

key_places.name: The Warm Winter
key_places.description: Not a place but an anomaly: the winter that ended the Sundering was unnaturally warm across the whole continent. The Reeve's archive holds the records. No one has explained it.

consequences: Per-age calendars: every realm counts years from this one.
The Glimmer replaces the song — magic becomes rare, feared, and expensive.
The Quiet becomes the world's defining wound and its slowest disaster.
The Censer is founded; containment becomes law for eight centuries.
The gods' silence begins — no verified divine contact since.
Old Weaver becomes dangerous knowledge; within eighty years it becomes contraband.
remembrance: Stilleven, the month of silence, re-enacts the year's end annually. The phrase 'since the world screamed once' means 'for as long as anyone can imagine'. Deep-folk mark it differently: their saga calls it 'the year the doors held'.
adventure_hooks: A 'silent walker' returns out of the Quiet after 812 years — alive, unaged, and asking for someone by name.
Players discover why the winter was warm. The answer is buried in three archives that hate each other.
The Rent's seam is measured again: this year it moved two hand-widths, not one. Nobody wants to be the one who reports it.
